identity.description: Max-margin kernel machine: solves a dual QP to find the separating surface (or ε-tube, SVR) defined by a subset of support vectors, with the RBF kernel lifting the boundary to be nonlinear. Strong on small-to-medium clean numeric data; fit cost over the n×n kernel matrix is its ceiling.

emits.note: the native output — sign of the decision function
decision_function margin (uncalibrated but well-ranked); also the SVR regression prediction

probability=True fits an INTERNAL Platt sigmoid on 5-fold CV — expensive at fit time, and its argmax can DISAGREE with predict() near the boundary; prefer the margin + an external calibrator on held-out data

gamma.note: rbf/poly/sigmoid only; 'scale' = 1/(p·Var(X)) is a strong default

epsilon.note: SVR only — the no-penalty tube width

probability.note: turns on the internal Platt CV; leave false and calibrate externally unless the probability port is wired

invariances.why: the RBF kernel exp(-γ‖x−x′‖²) is a unit-weighted distance — an unscaled high-variance feature owns the kernel, and a single shared γ cannot fit incomparable units
kernel values depend on actual coordinates, not order; a log-transform reshapes the kernel matrix and hence the margin
kernel evaluation on a missing coordinate is undefined; sklearn raises on NaN
kernels operate on numeric vectors; categoricals must be encoded first
margin maximization is geometric, not likelihood-based — no assumption on feature or error distributions

the dual QP works over an n×n kernel matrix — fit cost grows between O(n²) and O(n³); beyond a few tens of thousands of rows training becomes impractical (that regime belongs to linear/SGD or tree families)

with the RBF kernel every term exp(-γ‖x−sv‖²) vanishes far from the support vectors, so the decision function collapses to the bias — predictions saturate outside the data (linear kernel is the exception)

featureStats.why: the n×n kernel QP is the family's hard gate — fit time is the first thing to check before proposing an SVM
a shared γ over unscaled features means the kernel distance is owned by the highest-variance feature — the direct standardization signal
the hinge loss on a skewed problem is minimized by pushing the boundary into the minority class — flags class_weight='balanced' and PR-based metrics

modelMetrics.why: SVs approaching n means no margin structure was found (the model memorized the data); a compact SV set is the direct evidence the kernel geometry fits the problem
the internal Platt CV can make predict_proba's argmax disagree with predict() near the margin — a nonzero rate is the implementation-specific calibration-integrity warning to surface

edgeCases.behavior: QP fit time and kernel cache blow up superquadratically
edgeCases.note: route to linear/SGD or gradient-boosting families

edgeCases.behavior: kernel distance dominated by one feature; gamma='scale' only partly compensates
internal 5-fold Platt fit is unstable and 5x's fit cost
edgeCases.note: calibrate externally on held-out data instead

edgeCases.behavior: hinge loss degenerates toward the majority class

edgeCases.condition: C very large on noisy data
edgeCases.behavior: margin shrinks to fit noise — every noisy point becomes a support vector

driver.constructor: SVC(**hp) / SVR(**hp), selected by problem_type; probability=True only when the probability port is consumed
driver.serializationNote: artifact stores the support vectors — size scales with SV count, worst-case the whole training set

canBeSeeds.note: external isotonic/Platt on held-out data supersedes the internal probability=True machinery
the raw margin is the better stacking feature — monotone in confidence without the Platt squash

placementClaims.why: no native NaN handling — kernel evaluation is undefined on missing coordinates
not monotone-invariant: symmetrizing skewed features keeps a long tail from stretching the kernel distance along one axis
scale-sensitive by mechanism — a single γ over the RBF distance assumes comparable feature units
kernels need numeric input; categoricals must be encoded before fit
